root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: the `endp` argument passed to `vv->varint_get64s(&cp, ..., NULL)` equals `data + size`
root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `cram_varint_decode_init()` decodes `c->u.varint.offset`, the nested `varint_get64s()` call must use the declared codec-substream end `data + size` as its `endp` argument instead of `NULL`, so the second varint read stays bounded by the three-byte `HC` payload.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the second nested varint read with `end_argument == NULL` even though the outer parser already established a concrete substream end `data + size`. The fixed original passes that exact bound into the same call site.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable assertion trace records `offset_varint_root.end_argument=(nil)` while `offset_varint_root.substream_end=0x604000000779`, so the frozen equality is violated at the protected root event. The fixed original reaches the same event with `end_argument == substream_end == 0x604000000779`, making the required assertion genuine without perturbation.

nodes.state: Immediately after `c->u.varint.content_id = vv->varint_get32(&cp, NULL, NULL);`, the local `cp` cursor has already advanced beyond the declared codec-substream end `data + size`.

At the 9-byte `0xff` LTF8 sink branch, `safe_ltf8_get()` consumes the same already-advanced `*cp` value that `cram_varint_decode_init()` passed into the second nested varint read, so the subsequent `up[5]` load crosses the 48-byte heap block.

edges.relation: The exact `cp` cursor produced by the first nested `varint_get32()` call is carried unchanged into the following `varint_get64s()` call, so the second read starts from the already-overrun pointer state.
The same `cp` value passed into the vulnerable `vv->varint_get64s(&cp, ...)` call arrives at `safe_ltf8_get()`'s 9-byte `0xff` branch as `*cp`, so the sink reads from the already-advanced cursor.
